step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 41-year-old male presenting with painful cervical lymphadenopathy and arthralgia

step5_concept_grounding: Suspected diagnosis of Chikungunya evaluated in patient with necrotizing lymphadenitis and arthralgia

evidence_items.source_quote: The chikungunya IgM antibody was not detected by serum IgM ELISA.

step10_contradiction_notes: Clinicians made an unconfirmed clinical diagnosis of chikungunya based on history and symptoms, but disease-specific serum IgM ELISA was explicitly negative (not detected), failing the gold standard laboratory evidence requirement.
rationale: A 41-year-old male with painful cervical lymphadenopathy, fever, and later polyarthralgia. While clinicians posited a clinical diagnosis based on symptoms, specific laboratory testing was explicitly negative: 'The chikungunya IgM antibody was not detected by serum IgM ELISA' (E0 refuting/contradicted evidence). Under strict gold-standard curation rules, supportive symptoms (E3) in the presence of a negative specific assay fail VPD criteria. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 38-year-old male with expanded dengue syndrome and small-medium-vessel vasculitis

step5_concept_grounding: Chikungunya evaluated as differential diagnostic marker in acute febrile vasculitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood cultures turned out to be sterile, and other infectious markers (malaria, scrub typhus, and chikungunya) were negative, except for dengue serology (ELISA-IgM).

rationale: A 38-year-old male diagnosed with expanded dengue syndrome and vasculitis. Diagnostic workup specifically evaluated Chikungunya as an infectious marker and yielded negative results (E0 refuting evidence), ruling out Chikungunya coinfection. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case 4; 12-year-old male with fever, rash, and subsequently confirmed rickettsiosis

step5_concept_grounding: Initial clinical diagnosis of Chikungunya evaluated and contradicted by negative testing

evidence_items.source_quote: On this occasion, samples were taken to confirm chikungunya, yielding negative results.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial presumptive clinical diagnosis of chikungunya without lab confirmation was contradicted by negative laboratory tests on day 10 and subsequent positive serology for Rickettsia typhi.
rationale: A 12-year-old male was initially presumptively diagnosed with chikungunya clinically without testing. Upon re-evaluation on day 10, laboratory testing was performed to confirm chikungunya and yielded negative results (E0 contradictory evidence). The patient was subsequently confirmed to have Rickettsia typhi infection. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Previously healthy 45-year-old male traveler returning to the United Kingdom from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

evidence_items.source_quote: Results of serologic testing for chikungunya, dengue, and yellow fever were negative by commercial assays.

rationale: A 45-year-old male returning to the UK from Brazil presented with fever, retro-orbital headache, arthralgia, myalgia, and maculopapular rash. Commercial serological testing for chikungunya, dengue, and yellow fever was negative, while Zika virus RNA was detected in urine and semen and Zika IgM/IgG seroconverted. Chikungunya was explicitly ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 41-year-old immunocompetent male patient F.C.F. with Moraxella osloensis mitral valve endocarditis

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies were ordered for leptospirosis, rickettsialpox, hepatitis, syphilis, Zika virus, Chikungunya, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, toxoplasmosis, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). All of them had negative results.

rationale: A 41-year-old male presented with prolonged fever, weight loss, and mitral valve vegetation confirmed by three blood cultures as Moraxella osloensis infective endocarditis. Serology for Chikungunya was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 55-year-old male index patient in Kerala with West Nile virus-induced acute flaccid paralysis

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel was positive for WNV and negative for CMV, human herpes virus-6, rabies, John Cunningham virus, herpes simplex virus (HSV) 1 and 2, dengue, Japanese encephalitis (JE), nipah, chikungunya, chandipura, mumps, measles and enterovirus including poliovirus, fungi and bacteria including Myobacterium tuberculosis on day 7 (Xcyton acute encephalitis syndrome [AES], Bangalore).

rationale: A 55-year-old man presented with fever, meningoencephalitis, and acute flaccid quadriplegia. Day 7 CSF multiplex PCR panel (Xcyton AES) was negative for chikungunya and positive for West Nile virus (confirmed by WNV IgM and microneutralization titer 40). Chikungunya was explicitly ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old male with seronegative rheumatoid arthritis on abatacept and right prosthetic hip infection due to Mycobacterium avium complex

evidence_items.source_quote: The following infection diagnostics were negative: malaria smear and Ag, HIV ag/Ab, Syphilis Ab, Histoplasma serum Ag and Ab, Coccidiodes serology, Cryptococcal serum Ag, Bartonella and Brucella IgG/IgM, T spot TB, Chikungunya IgG and 2 sets of blood cultures.

rationale: A 56-year-old male presented with fever of unknown origin and right hip pain after travel to Honduras. Chikungunya IgG serology was negative, and right hip aspirate and tissue AFB cultures grew Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC). Chikungunya was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 27-year-old pregnant mother and her 35-week stillborn male fetus (46, XY) with Congenital Zika Syndrome; CSF triplex RT-PCR performed on the stillborn fetus detected Zika viral RNA only

evidence_items.source_quote: The RT-PCR for ZIKV/Dengue/Chikungunya in the patient's cerebrospinal fluid detected the presence of Zika viral RNA.

rationale: In a case of Congenital Zika Syndrome with fetal brain disruption sequence, arthrogryposis, and right forearm absence in a 35-week stillborn fetus of a 27-year-old woman, CSF RT-PCR for ZIKV/Dengue/Chikungunya detected Zika viral RNA only, ruling out Chikungunya -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old white male with fatal vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) following ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination

evidence_items.source_quote: SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR of the nasopharyngeal swab and serology to dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, HIV, hepatitis B and C, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), toxoplasmosis, and rubella were negative.

rationale: A 56-year-old male developed fatal vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) with anti-PF4 antibodies after ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination. Serology for Chikungunya was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Male patient from Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil (abstract states 'He presented symptoms of fever, myalgia and headache') with DENV-2 and yellow fever virus coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: multiplex qRT-PCR composed of two platforms to determine the virus (platform A: four viral serotypes of dengue, yellow fever, Zika, chikungunya; and platform B: Mayaro, Rocio, St Louis and West Nile) was performed in an ABI 7500 thermal cycler.
In multiplex qRT-PCR, genetic material from DENV2 and YFV was detected.

rationale: A patient in Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil presented with fever, myalgia, and headache and underwent serum multiplex qRT-PCR testing covering dengue serotypes 1-4, yellow fever, Zika, and chikungunya (Platform A). Only DENV-2 and YFV genetic material was detected, ruling out chikungunya -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 53-year-old hypertensive female with expanded dengue syndrome presenting as basal ganglia hemorrhage, fever, and rhabdomyolysis

evidence_items.source_quote: On account of a history of fever with chill and myalgia around a week before ED admission, a tropical workup was sent for malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, dengue, chikungunya, and scrub typhus, in which serology (IgM antibodies) for dengue turned out to be positive.

rationale: A 53-year-old female with basal ganglia intracranial hemorrhage, high-grade fever, and rhabdomyolysis underwent a tropical fever panel for malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, dengue, chikungunya, and scrub typhus, in which only dengue IgM antibodies were positive (confirming expanded dengue syndrome and ruling out chikungunya) -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 49-year-old female with fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock supported with Impella CP

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and biopsy specimens were tested for common causative agents, such as Coxsackieviruses A and B, echoviruses, polioviruses, influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, mumps virus, measles virus, rubella virus, hepatitis C virus, dengue virus, yellow fever virus, Chikungunya virus, human immunodeficiency virus-1, adenoviruses, parvovirus B19, cytomegalovirus, human herpes virus-6, Epstein-Barr virus, varicella-zoster virus, and herpes simplex virus, as recommended, but none of these triggers was detected.
evidence_items.test_name: Viral PCR on EDTA blood and endomyocardial biopsy

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral PCR (polymerase chain reaction) in RNA-stabilized EMB and EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) blood demonstrated absence of infectious causative organisms.

rationale: A 49-year-old female presented with fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock. Viral PCR testing of EDTA blood and right ventricular endomyocardial biopsy for Chikungunya virus and other viral pathogens detected no infectious organisms -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 15-year-old girl with dengue fever-associated hemophagocytic syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: She tested negative for malaria, HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C virus, and chikungunya.

rationale: A 15-year-old girl presented with 7 days of high-grade fever, arthralgia, myalgia, pancytopenia, and hemophagocytic syndrome confirmed as dengue fever by positive dengue NS1 antigen and IgM. She explicitly tested negative for chikungunya -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old pregnant Canadian traveler infected with Zika virus in Trinidad at 9 weeks gestation

evidence_items.source_quote: Her blood tested negative in Trinidad by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for dengue and chikungunya viruses, but was positive for ZIKV.
Dengue IgM and IgG were reactive, and chikungunya IgM and IgG were non-reactive.

rationale: A 29-year-old pregnant Canadian traveler developed fever and rash in Trinidad with confirmed maternal and fetal Zika virus infection. Blood real-time RT-PCR for chikungunya virus at day 7 was negative and serum chikungunya IgM and IgG at day 30 were non-reactive -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Woman in her mid-twenties presenting with scrub typhus, abdominal eschar, and moderate ARDS

evidence_items.source_quote: Card tests for dengue fever and chikungunya were negative.

rationale: A woman in her mid-twenties presented with high-grade fever, abdominal eschar, and ARDS confirmed as scrub typhus by positive Weil-Felix (1:640 OX-K) and Orientia tsutsugamushi IgM (1:160). Card tests for dengue fever and chikungunya were explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old pregnant woman in Brazil with Zika-associated Guillain-Barre syndrome and missed abortion at 15 weeks gestation

evidence_items.source_quote: The IgM serology for Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, Epstein Barr and Cytomegalovirus were non-reactive (in further sections of this paper, diagnosis of ZIKV infection was confirmed by specific staining in placental and fetal tissues).

rationale: A 28-year-old pregnant woman presented with Guillain-Barre syndrome and retained fetal demise at 15 weeks gestation, with Zika virus confirmed by placental and fetal tissue immunostaining. Maternal IgM serology for Chikungunya was non-reactive -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 9-month-old male infant (input metadata age 0.0) with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, toxic epidermal necrolysis/Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and CMV infection

evidence_items.source_quote: Work up done for infectious etiology including blood culture, urine culture, malarial antigen test, serology for dengue, chikungunya, leptospirosis, and rickettsia was negative.

rationale: A 9-month-old boy developed fatal hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis associated with Stevens-Johnson syndrome/TEN, whole blood transfusion, and CMV viruria. Serology for chikungunya was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 21-year-old pregnant woman (Case 3) with second-trimester Zika virus infection confirmed by IgM and PRNT90%

evidence_items.source_quote: Her IgM serology for ZIKV was positive and non-reactive for dengue, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV, syphilis and cytomegalovirus.

rationale: In Case 3 of a maternal Zika placental study, a 21-year-old pregnant woman with second-trimester fever had positive ZIKV IgM and PRNT90%, while IgM serology for chikungunya was explicitly non-reactive -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 24-year-old pregnant woman (Case 7) who delivered a male infant with microcephaly and ventriculomegaly (input metadata lists Male from the newborn boy)

evidence_items.source_quote: Her IgM serology for dengue, herpes, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV and cytomegalovirus were non-reactive.

rationale: In Case 7 of a maternal Zika placental study, a 24-year-old pregnant patient with second-trimester exanthema and pruritus had non-reactive IgM serology for chikungunya -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old pregnant woman (Case 10) with third-trimester fever who delivered a male infant with microcephaly and arthrogryposis (input metadata lists Male from the newborn boy)

evidence_items.source_quote: Her IgM serology for dengue, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV, syphilis and cytomegalovirus were non-reactive, and positive for ZIKV.

rationale: In Case 10 of a maternal Zika placental study, a 28-year-old pregnant woman with third-trimester fever tested positive for ZIKV IgM while her IgM serology for chikungunya was explicitly non-reactive -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 7-year-old boy in Bandung, West Java, Indonesia with dengue virus serotype 1 encephalitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Other classical neurotropic pathogens including Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), chikungunya virus, human herpesviruses, enteroviruses, Streptococcus pneumonia and Haemophilus influenzae were negative using PCR testing algorithms   as well as an anti-JEV IgM assay.

rationale: A 7-year-old boy in Indonesia presented with dengue encephalitis confirmed by DENV-1 RT-PCR in CSF and serum and anti-DENV IgM/IgG seroconversion. PCR testing for chikungunya virus was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 25-year-old male farmer in western Kenya with fatal Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests in Nairobi were negative for yellow fever, dengue, West Nile, Chikungunya, and Rift Valley fever (immunoglobulin [Ig] M-capture enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) and reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) tests for flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Bunyamwera serogroup bunyaviruses were also negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Chikungunya IgM-capture ELISA and alphavirus RT-PCR

rationale: A 25-year-old male farmer in Kenya died of acute viral hemorrhagic fever confirmed by RT-PCR and sequencing as Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (C-CHFV). Both IgM-capture ELISA for Chikungunya and RT-PCR for alphaviruses were negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 17-year-old Kenyan female with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis

evidence_items.source_quote: We immediately ran investigations comprehensive blood and/or urine tests for infection, auto-immune disease (including vasculitis) and toxic causes (including porphyria), also comprising polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for tropical fever pathogens (human immunodeficiency virus, Treponema pallidum, malaria, Leptospira, rickettsia, dengue, West Nile, chikungunya and rabies viruses - with additional testing in saliva and neck hairline skin biopsies for the latter), contrast-enhanced computed tomography scan of the head, chest and abdomen which were all normal/negative.

rationale: A 17-year-old Kenyan female was diagnosed with autoimmune anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis (positive NMDA receptor antibodies in serum and CSF). PCR testing for tropical fever pathogens including chikungunya virus was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 43-year-old Australian male returning from Bali, Indonesia with acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP)

evidence_items.source_quote: He had negative serologies over the initial week for the following infections: streptococcus, syphilis, Ross River virus, Barmah Forest virus, alphavirus, Rickettsia rickettsii, measles, mumps, leptospirosis, parvovirus B19, enterovirus, varicella and HIV.

rationale: A 43-year-old man returning to Australia from Bali presented with fever, arthralgia, and generalized pustular rash clinically diagnosed as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) triggered by cold medication/ibuprofen. Retrieval matched on the genus term 'alphavirus', and serologies for Ross River virus, Barmah Forest virus, and alphavirus were all explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 14-year-old male adolescent with pediatric chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) and anti-neurofascin 155 IgG4 antibodies

evidence_items.source_quote: An infectious cause was ruled out from negative blood serologies (HIV, Lyme, EBV, E. coli, Campylobacter, CMV, Mycoplasma, Chikungunya, Zika, hepatitis E) and a broad range PCR in the CSF.

rationale: A 14-year-old boy with severe pediatric CIDP and anti-NF155 IgG4 autoantibodies had infectious causes explicitly ruled out by negative blood serologies including Chikungunya and negative CSF broad-range PCR -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 1-year-and-8-month-old male child with neurological manifestations of Brazilian spotted fever (input metadata lists Female, but case_text explicitly states 'Male patient, 1 year and 8 months old')

evidence_items.source_quote: On the same day, CSF fluid was also tested for Rickettsia spp., herpesvirus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, meningococcus and pneumococcus, by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay.
All other PCR tests were negative.

rationale: A 20-month-old boy in Brazil with tick exposure, fever, petechial rash, aphasia, and left hemiparesis was confirmed to have Brazilian spotted fever (Rickettsia spp. PCR positive on admission sample and seroconversion IgM 1/512, IgG 1/128). CSF PCR testing for chikungunya virus was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Adult patient with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) following COVID-19 and concomitant CMV viremia

evidence_items.source_quote: Initial evaluation included serology for the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), toxoplasma, rubeola, CMV, herpes simplex virus 1 and 2 (HSV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Coxiella, hepatitis A, B, C, and E virus, Leptospira, Bartonella, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and Brucella, which were negative for recent or current infection.

rationale: An adult patient diagnosed with post-COVID-19 multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) and CMV reactivation underwent initial serological testing for chikungunya, which was negative for recent or current infection -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 65-year-old Canadian male with Lyme disease (erythema migrans and CN VII and XII palsies) following travel to Ecuador

evidence_items.source_quote: A broad infectious work up, including blood and urine cultures, respiratory virus PCR, malaria thick and thin blood smear and rapid diagnostic test, and serologic testing for Hepatitis A, B, C, and E, Dengue virus, Chikungunya virus, West Nile virus, Yellow Fever, Rickettsia (spotted fever and typhi), and Trypanosome cruzi, were negative.

rationale: A 65-year-old Canadian man presented with erythema migrans and cranial nerve VII and XII palsies confirmed as Lyme disease by modified two-tier Borrelia burgdorferi serology. Serologic testing for Chikungunya virus was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 34-year-old Asian male with Adult-Onset Still's Disease (AOSD)

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral and zoonotic serologies, including dengue, chikungunya, leptospirosis, brucellosis, typhoid, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and hepatitis A, B, and C, were all negative.
Extensive serological testing excluded dengue, chikungunya, leptospirosis, brucellosis, typhoid, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and viral hepatitis.

rationale: A 34-year-old man presented with quotidian high-grade fevers, symmetric polyarthralgia, sore throat, and marked hyperferritinemia (6,900 ng/mL) diagnosed as Adult-Onset Still's Disease. Serological testing for chikungunya was explicitly negative -> NEGATIVE.
